skills.name: Concord: agreement with the grammatical subject

note.text: The finite verb agrees with the grammatical subject in the taught present patterns. In the chair of the groups, chair is the singular nucleus; groups is inside a complement. Each of the reporters takes singular agreement in the model. Distinct subjects Bih and Ayuk joined by and take plural agreement. A nearby plural noun does not automatically control the verb. Collective nouns and some coordinated constructions vary according to meaning and convention; the exercises use explicit cases rather than treating every collective expression alike.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to choose a present verb agreeing with its subject despite an intervening complement or a coordinated subject. Builds on: sentence structure, quantifiers and the revised verb forms. Leads to: editing formal and informal letters.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original models: The chair of the groups {thirdPerson("write")} the summary. The members of the club write it. Each of the reporters {thirdPerson("check")} a detail. Bih and Ayuk prepare the notice. The complements do not replace the subject, and a participle alone does not provide a missing finite verb.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Mark the whole subject, find its nucleus or coordination, then choose the present form. Check that an apparent correction has not changed tense. Read the full clause rather than matching the last noun to the nearest verb.

cards.idea: A correction must preserve the intended meaning and form.
example: Groups must control the verb simply because it is nearer. Correction: The nearer noun is inside a complement.
Each of the reporters always requires check without the singular marker. Correction: Each controls singular agreement here.
Two distinct named subjects here require prepares. Correction: The coordination is plural in the stated model.
The members writing alone gives the complete finite model. Correction: The -ing form needs an appropriate auxiliary to make that progressive clause.
